subject: Request: Conservative canary + automatic fallback as SLA mitigation for Medisys go-live
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@medisys.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production readiness — canary fallback / pinning to meet SLA

Marcus,

We're roughly two weeks from our cutover and the platform team at Medisys has raised a hard ask: because their patient-facing flows are latency-sensitive, they want an explicit SLA mitigation that gives them: (1) an automatic, measurable fallback to the previous stable model if latency or error rates spike during an A/B/canary, and (2) the ability to pin traffic to a verified stable model for short windows while we investigate.

Specifically they asked for guidance on thresholds (latency ms, error rate), automatic actions (fallback, pin duration), and any contractual carveouts we need to sign off on. They also want a short playbook for on-call if the canary starts degrading user experience.

I've attached our current mutual action plan (Medisys_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf) — can your team confirm whether Redwood can support auto-fallback + temporary pins under our hosted SLA? If yes, what exact telemetry/thresholds do you recommend and what approvals do we need from Redwood?

Thanks,

Carlos Vega
Head of Platform
Medisys Health

Attachment: Medisys_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@medisys.io>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production readiness — canary fallback / pinning to meet SLA

Looping you in — Medisys (DEAL-4982) is asking for an operational SLA mitigation tied to their canary/A-B rollout. They want: automatic fallback to prior model variant on degradation + the ability to pin to a stable variant for troubleshooting windows.

My proposed conservative approach (to both protect their UX and keep us within our SLA guarantees):
- Canary weight: start at 1% for 30m, then 5% for 60m, then 10% for 2h (customer can opt more aggressive).
- Auto-fallback triggers (fail-open policy):
  - p50 latency increase > 120ms above baseline sustained for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows OR
  - error ratio (5xx / total) > 0.8% for 5 minutes OR
  - inference timeout rate > 0.2% for 2 minutes.
- Auto action: immediate traffic swap back to pinned stable variant (automated rollback).
- Pin duration after fallback: default 30 minutes (manual release or extended pin via SRE approval).
- Telemetry: 1s granularity traces for latency, 10m retention minimum in console; detailed logs retained 90d for postmortem.
- Contractual: we can include a limited SLA carveout that allows an automated canary fallback without triggering credits, provided Medisys follows the agreed canary plan and runbook.

Can you confirm that engineering/sre are comfortable implementing these thresholds and the pin behavior? If so I will send a follow-up to Carlos with the playbook and DocuSign MMP for signatures.

Thanks — Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@medisys.io>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production readiness — canary fallback / pinning to meet SLA

Marcus — thanks for laying this out. This looks reasonable from a product and sales perspective. A couple of notes/conditions before we sign off internally: 

1) Security & compliance: we need an explicit SRE-run security checklist for the canary (no PII sampling in logs, sampling policy documented).
2) Runbook: attach a concise playbook that operations can run through — must include the communication steps (who to page, escalation timeline).
3) Manual override guardrail: there must be a manual kill-switch in Console to immediately disable auto-fallback (in case of cascading failures caused by the fallback itself).
4) Telemetry retention: 90d log retention is fine but we need the ability to export traces to Medisys for an investigation within 72 hours of request.

If engineering confirms they can implement the triggers you proposed, I approve the customer communication and the DocuSign MMP flow. Please attach the playbook and the MMP signature request and i'll push it through legal for a quick review.

- Lauren
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

> On Mon, Mar 29, 2027 at 10:03 AM Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Looping you in — Medisys is asking for an operational SLA mitigation...
From: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@medisys.io>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production readiness — canary fallback / pinning to meet SLA

Marcus/Team — I reviewed the thresholds with SRE. We can implement the auto-fallback and pin behavior, with the following operational constraints: 

- SRE will deploy a canary supervisor that evaluates the triggers you proposed. We recommend tightening two thresholds to be extra conservative for a healthcare customer:
  • p50 latency increase > 100ms sustained for 2 mins (instead of 120ms / 3x1m)
  • error ratio > 0.5% for 3 mins (instead of 0.8% / 5m)
- Pin duration: default 30m is OK, but SRE requires a mandatory post-fallback incident review within 24 hours; automated extensions will require approval from on-call SRE.
- Manual kill-switch: implemented in Console, as requested; only SRE & RBAC-admin role can disable auto-fallback.
- Playbook: attached (canary_playbook_v2.docx) — covers steps for rollback, communications, and escalation matrix.

Provided we agree to the tightened thresholds above and Medisys signs the MMP (DocuSign link to follow), i am happy to sign off from SRE.

Grace Oconnor
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: canary_playbook_v2.docx

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Confirmation & next steps — Medisys canary safeguards and MMP

Carlos — thanks for patience. Quick summary and next steps from Redwood: 

Summary of agreed approach (conservative canary + automatic fallback):
- Canary plan: 1% (30m) -> 5% (60m) -> 10% (2h).
- Triggers that will cause automated fallback to the pinned stable variant (SRE-enforced):
  - p50 latency increase > 100ms sustained for 2 minutes
  - error ratio > 0.5% for 3 continuous minutes
  - inference timeout > 0.2% for 2 continuous minutes
- Auto-action: immediate automated traffic swap to prior pinned stable variant. Pin remains in place 30 minutes by default; SRE will run a mandatory post-fallback review within 24 hours.
- Manual guardrail: Console kill-switch exists (RBAC-protected) to disable auto-fallback if necessary.
- Observability: 1s latency traces; 90d logs; export package available within 72 hours on request.

Next steps:
1) I'm attaching SRE playbook (canary_playbook_v2.docx) and the MMP signature request (MMP-signature-request.docusign).
2) If Medisys OKs the tightened SRE thresholds above, please sign the DocuSign MMP — the DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/link/XYZ-4982
3) Upon signature, SRE will schedule a dry-run in our staging region and confirm the canary supervisor config.

Carlos, please reply-all with a thumbs up and expected signature ETA and we'll move forward with scheduling.

Best,

Marcus Lin
